company_items.summary: Costco reported September comps with US core (ex-FX and gas) up 8%, approximately 80 basis points above consensus and a sharp acceleration from the +5.6% posted in August. This is a high-quality beat driven by underlying consumer demand, not one-time items. The acceleration is a strong positive signal for the consumer spending environment.

Levi reported FQ3 EPS of 48 cents versus the Street's 36-cent estimate, but the bulk of the outperformance came from tariff refunds — ex those refunds, EPS was roughly 37 cents, essentially inline. Tariff refunds provided a 330 basis point tailwind to operating margins and a 370 basis point tailwind to gross margins. Full-year EPS guidance was raised to $1.54-$1.56 from $1.46-$1.52, and organic revenue growth guidance moves to +6% from +5.5-6%, though DTC and US revenue were soft in the quarter with management noting a recent reacceleration heading into holiday.

Lululemon's new CEO announced a refreshed leadership team, naming Maggie Gauger — formerly President and CEO of Athleta — as President and Chief Product Officer, and Joseph Godsey from Walmart Canada as Chief Operating Officer, both newly created roles. Nikki Neuburger and Ted Dagnese are departing the company. Searches are underway for Chief Brand Officer, Chief Communications Officer, and Chief Technology Officer roles, signaling the organization remains in transition.

The Department of War's Office of Strategic Capital announced a $1.5 billion conditional loan commitment to Wolfspeed. This is a significant capital infusion from the government that could help stabilize the company's balance sheet and support its silicon carbide semiconductor manufacturing buildout. The conditionality of the loan means execution milestones will matter.

tts_summary:
Here's your after-market rundown for Wednesday, October 7th. This note is focused entirely on company-specific earnings and news — no broad macro or Fed commentary tonight, so let's get right into it.

First up, Costco. September comps came in strong, with US core sales — that's ex-fuel and foreign exchange — up 8%. That's about 80 basis points above what the Street was expecting and a sharp acceleration from the plus 5.6% posted in August. This is a clean, high-quality beat. No accounting tricks, just consumers showing up and spending. Bullish read for the consumer broadly.

Next, Levi Strauss. The headline EPS print was 48 cents versus the Street at 36 cents — looks like a massive beat. But here's the catch: strip out tariff refunds and you're at 37 cents, essentially inline. Those refunds were a 330 basis point tailwind to operating margins and a 370 basis point tailwind to gross margins, so the quality of the beat is questionable. Revenue was a touch light due to weakness in direct-to-consumer and the US. The good news is management says DTC trends have reaccelerated recently heading into holiday. Full-year EPS guidance moved up to $1.54 to $1.56 from $1.46 to $1.52, and organic revenue growth guidance ticks up to 6%. This one's mixed — real underlying results were fine, not great, but the guide-up is a positive.

Lululemon. The new CEO is putting their stamp on the leadership team fast. They've hired Maggie Gauger — formerly President and CEO of Athleta — as President and Chief Product Officer, and brought in Joseph Godsey from Walmart Canada as Chief Operating Officer. Both are newly created roles. Meanwhile, two existing executives are out the door: the Chief Brand and Product Activation Officer and the Chief Supply Chain Officer. And searches are still underway for a Chief Brand Officer, Chief Communications Officer, and Chief Technology Officer. That's a lot of open seats. Hiring the top exec from Athleta is interesting — it's a competitor, though not the one investors fear most, which would be Vuori or ALO. Hard to call this clearly good or bad, but the level of organizational churn heading into the holiday season creates real execution risk. Call it mixed with a cautious lean.

Finally, Wolfspeed. The Department of War's Office of Strategic Capital announced a 1.5 billion dollar conditional loan commitment to the company. This is meaningful government backing for their silicon carbide semiconductor manufacturing push. The conditionality matters — they'll need to hit milestones — but this is a clear positive for a company that has had significant capital structure concerns.

Bottom line tonight: consumer spending looks resilient based on Costco's numbers. Levi was fine once you normalize for one-time tariff items. Lululemon is a show-me story in the middle of a leadership overhaul. And Wolfspeed got a major lifeline. Stay sharp.
